title: Rashomon: three voices
subtitle: Legitimacy battlefield · round one
intro: The purge begins. Three complete testimonies, and the archive can only file one first. No judge, only whoever gets written in first.
closing: The three accounts tear at each other. The archive keeps them; the truth is not kept.

rounds.label: Round one · filing
rounds.prompt: The purge begins. Three complete testimonies on the table, and the archive can only file one first. Who speaks first?

choices.label: Anti-Gotō: Gotō approached the press himself
choices.detail: It reads most like an accusation, and is most easily called taking sides by the Ji camp.
choices.result: Her version enters the file. The Ji camp says at once: this is a Gotō-camp purge.

choices.label: Gotō: I was only put on the masthead
choices.detail: It protects his position and also the part he won't admit.
choices.result: Gotō's version writes him as a passive man. The file is stable; the question is not.

choices.label: Muyu: I did want to destroy the od scene
choices.detail: The ugliest to hear, and the least like a weapon for either side.
choices.result: Muyu's testimony offends both sides. For the first time the file holds a sentence that takes no side.

rounds.label: Round two · the ending
rounds.prompt: The three testimonies bite into each other. The ending can only be written one way.

choices.label: Set all three side by side, no verdict
choices.detail: Keep the contradictions exactly as they are.
choices.result: The file is thicker and harder for any side to cite. Readers have to judge for themselves.

choices.label: Write only what can be verified
choices.detail: Take out every sentence that can't be checked.
choices.result: The file gets thinner, but every sentence can be checked. All three voices come out incomplete.

choices.label: Hand the contradictions to the public as they are
choices.detail: End it for no one; let everyone see three mouths.
choices.result: The public gets three testimonies that slap each other. People start saying: even they can't agree.

reactions.fan: The Ji camp cuts the anti-Gotō testimony into a "purge manifesto". The Gotō camp starts demanding you add Gotō's name.
reactions.goto: Gotō's version lets the Gotō camp breathe. The Ji camp asks: why can a man only on the masthead speak for the archive?
reactions.muyu: Muyu's testimony offends both sides. Both start asking: should this part be cut?
